actualProducerData.tableConstruction: Request: common 11 + request literals 35 + CORS 3 + appended Content-Length 1 = 50. actualProducerData.retainedArrayWidths: Request primary 4, response primary 5, request-existence 3, request-count 1, response-existence 5, enhanced 5, invalid H2/H3 response 5; formatted-internal 7 of which 6 pseudo identifiers. Five pseudo identifiers occur in the request table; Status does not.
actualProducerData.apiNameProducer: HeaderNames declares 96 public static readonly string fields. Five are Obsolete and excluded by the reflection filter, leaving 91 field names. NonApiHeaders has 9 distinct entries formed from two nonpublic wire names plus seven internal identifiers; among the 91 defined public field names only DNT is removed, leaving 90 API names.
actualProducerData.duplicateContract: WebSocketSubProtocols and SecWebSocketProtocol have the same wire value, but DefinedHeaderNames selects field names, so both field-name API entries survive. NonApiHeaders mixes the Alt-Used wire value with the AltUsed identifier; neither is silently normalized.

calculationLimits: Literal cardinalities and complete-pass counts are source arithmetic, not measured operation counts or elapsed/allocation predictions.
Sequential-equality-position bounds do not assert the implementation of the selected runtime Enumerable.Contains or string operations.
No culture-sensitive sorting or reflection is executed. Table data are unsorted source literals; indexes/masks are read from the pinned checked-in generated output.
Existing generated output was statically checked for expected field/property membership; this is not executing the generator or the GeneratedCodeIsUpToDate test.

contracts.equality: All contested string Contains calls omit a comparer and use default string equality, which is ordinal and case-sensitive. Any membership index must match that equality; runtime header case-insensitivity elsewhere is not permission to use OrdinalIgnoreCase here. Identifier matching is against resolved field-name identifiers, not raw wire-name text.
contracts.ordering: Keep existing primary-first OrderBy and ThenBy(header => header), whose default string ordering is culture-sensitive; keep index assignments and Content-Length special indices. ApiHeaderNames originates from reflection field names and Except; preserve the existing ApiHeaderNames sequence when emitting F259 fallback properties. Do not enumerate a replacement set to emit source. The offline derivation does not execute reflection or culture-sensitive sorting.
contracts.duplicates: Membership does not require duplicate output removal. Preserve original table arrays and original API field-name sequence; Except already has its own distinct/default-equality behavior. Deduplicating by wire values would incorrectly collapse the two WebSocket API aliases.
contracts.mutation: Readonly array fields do not make array elements immutable. FormattedInternalHeaderNames elements have read-only properties but the public array elements can be replaced. KnownHeader exposes mutable Name, ClassName, Index, byte metadata and flags. No selected normal producer changes Name during filtering; only byte metadata writes are observed during GeneratedFile. That observation is not a universal prohibition on mutation.
contracts.enumeration: F258 ToArray/Aggregate executes the selected initialization pipelines; do not turn a membership cache into the emitted-table producer. F259 Each first calls Any on the filtered API sequence and then enumerates it again through Select/Aggregate. Full passes make 267 membership predicates, plus 3 to 87 additional Any-prefix memberships independent of reflection ordering. The source-order output agrees with the checked-in fallback sequence, but actual runtime reflection enumeration was not executed.
contracts.exceptions: Current literal producers resolve to non-null strings and the two no-seed Aggregate bit queries are nonempty (five matches each). If generalized or externally mutated to empty/null data, existing Aggregate/Identifier resolution can throw. Eager set materialization changes evaluation time, short-circuit reachability, and potentially exception ordering for malformed or concurrently mutated arrays. Do not claim arbitrary mutable-input exception equivalence from these literal-source checks.
contracts.concurrency: No concurrent generator/table mutation path is established in the selected normal producers. Public mutable tables and += byte-state writes mean thread-safe concurrent generation is not established either. No locks, new concurrency model, or global cache is proposed.
contracts.resultBoundary: These are source contracts and static consistency checks against captured output, not red/green execution or proof of arbitrary caller behavior.

distinctDecisions.decisionReason: The repeated-lookup shape is retained, including the PseudoRequestHeadersBits projection. At the actual literal sizes it performs 542 membership calls per successful type initialization, with 1..7-element retained sources and a conservative 2547 sequential-equality-position bound plus at most 350 pseudo-filter item visits. It also initializes for actual Core.Tests data production, so generator-only dismissal is incorrect. There is no source-backed multiplicative request/header-row frequency and no observed materiality basis for adding a family of membership structures.
distinctDecisions.sourceOnlyAlternative: If later owner evidence shows meaningful aggregate type-initialization cost, consider only local membership preparation in the initializer while preserving all source arrays, ordering, flags and masks. Do not blindly replace the width-one check or add permanent global sets for tiny arrays.
distinctDecisions.notClaimed: This is not a measured no-gain result, a rejection merely because work is build/test-time, or runtime/performance qualification. No native gate was consumed.

distinctDecisions.decisionReason: This is a distinct per-GeneratedFile API-complement calculation, not an alias of static table construction. The actual three loop tables are 50/39/3 and the API producer is 90 field names. Each complete emission pass checks 89 non-ContentLength API names per loop, hence 267 membership calls and a conservative 8188 projected-Identifier-visit bound, plus Each.Any prefix work. Identifier recomputation is real source work via ResolveIdentifier, although no allocation or timing amount was measured.
distinctDecisions.finiteProposal: For the supported unmodified literal-table producer, prepare one ephemeral ordinal identifier-membership index for each actual loop and use it only to answer F259 membership. Keep ApiHeaderNames as the outer producer, the ContentLength exclusion, the original three loops and every array/order/duplicate/output contract. Do not share F258 state or cache identifiers statically across calls.
requiredBeforeImplementation: Resolve whether externally mutated/reentrant/concurrent KnownHeader.Name inputs are supported. Eager projection does not preserve every short-circuit exception or mutation observation; this source pass does not authorize changing those contracts.

After separate approval, compare the full real GeneratedFile/Program.Run output from an unmodified owning producer against its checked-in baseline and cover special ContentLength, internal/pseudo names, and both WebSocket alias field names. Do not test just an isolated membership helper.

If materiality is pursued, use the actual single producer invocation/test lifecycle with exact real inputs and account for index construction. Do not pad API/header tables, repeat the stateful generator to manufacture a workload, or infer a server-throughput benefit.
distinctDecisions.notClaimed: No candidate, source edit, generator run, correctness pass, throughput/allocation improvement, or runtime qualification exists. This proposal is a finite next gate for the parent, not execution authority.
